Primary Care Progress Note

Patient: Ahmed Gerlach, 84-year-old male

Subjective:
Mr. Gerlach presents for his routine follow-up appointment. He reports feeling generally well with no new complaints today.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurological exams are unremarkable.

Assessment:
Mr. Gerlach is an elderly male in stable condition. There are no new findings or concerns at this time.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any new symptoms arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/18/2026

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/25/2026
Patient: Ahmed Gerlach, 84-year-old male

History of Present Illness:
Back pain began 08/08/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 7 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 7/10 despite 6 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 23/24.

Management:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Given the persistent pain and disability, consideration for spine intervention is appropriate. Further imaging and evaluation will guide treatment options.

Plan:
Continue current pain management and brace use. Schedule follow-up after intervention planning. Monitor for any signs of infection or neurological changes.
